cohort: Women with singleton pregnancies, categorized into those with major fetal anomalies and a control group with non-anomalous fetuses, from a tertiary university hospital over a 10-year period.
finding: Major fetal anomalies were significantly associated with an increased likelihood of adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes, including lower gestational age at delivery, higher rates of preterm delivery, placental abruption, cesarean section, postpartum hemorrhage, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, stillbirth, and neonatal death.
mod_finding: Cesarean section rates were significantly higher in pregnancies with major fetal anomalies (53.8%) compared to the control group (28.3%).
gest_age: Median gestational age at delivery was 37.0 weeks for pregnancies with anomalies and 39.4 weeks for controls; preterm delivery rates were higher at < 37 weeks (46.2% vs 6.2%) and < 32 weeks (15.4% vs 1.2%).
